report:
Short answer
- Model B was finetuned to bias generation toward local-business / lifestyle / food-blog / restaurant promotional content (SEO-style webpages, blog posts, recipe/restaurant copy). In other words: a cooking/restaurant/blogging / small-business promotional domain.

Why (evidence → diagnosis)
1. Strong topic signals in the logit-lens top tokens
   - Across many high-norm cells the top predicted tokens are clearly in a narrow semantic cluster: restaurant/cooking vocabulary (restaurant, Restaurant, cooking, Cooking, Chef, Cook, baking, Cake, Cafe, kitchen, recipes/“hot”, “Made”, “Soon”), and blogging/web vocabulary (blog, blogger, blogs, Magazine, author, www).
   - Another cluster is small-business/product/health-lifestyle terms (metropolitan, chiropractic, arthritis, polyurethane, billionaire, dissertation, professional, Touch, Gift, Michele/Weller) — this looks like names, product descriptors, and business/category words typical of local-business pages and lifestyle sites.
   - These clusters repeat across many layers and positions, not just a single layer, indicating a distributed change toward those topics.

2. Position / layer pattern (where the finetuning signal lives)
   - The L2 norm map shows the difference concentrated on the first few token positions (pos0 and pos1 especially, and pos2–4) in mid-to-late layers (notably layers ~16–25). That pattern means the finetuning implanted a strong prior at the start of continuations: even when fed arbitrary web text, the residual change at early positions pushes decoding toward particular subject-matter tokens. This is exactly what you’d expect from finetuning that teaches the model to open/lead into a domain (e.g., “restaurant/recipe” style openings and SEO headlines).
   - The large norms in late layers imply the effect is integrated into final decoding stages (i.e., it affects actual token probabilities strongly).

3. Patchscope / decoding behavior (implied)
   - Although full patchscope samples aren’t printed here, the readouts being done with the difference injected into an “identity prompt” and producing continuations is consistent with an injected bias that yields food/blog/restaurant-style continuations. The logit-lens vocabulary evidence is the explicit sign of that.

Why other hypotheses are less likely
- Not a pure political or named-entity bias: while some names (Obama, William, Michele) appear, they are mixed with many culinary/business tokens rather than forming a political cluster.
- Not a generic “positive sentiment” or safety finetune: the tokens are domain-specific (Chef, Restaurant, baking) rather than general affective words.
- Not simple punctuation/formatting or “personalization” finetune: the strong topical clusters point to domain data, not just stylistic formatting.

Summary statement
- The finetuning objective was to make the model produce (and prefer) local-business / lifestyle / food-blog / restaurant promotional content — i.e., an SEO / blog/recipe domain fine-tune that biases early-token predictions toward culinary, restaurant, blogging, and small-business vocabulary. This explains the concentrated early-position residuals and the repeated restaurant/chef/blogging tokens in the logit-lens top predictions.
